public_rationale: Assessing the prediction as 'largely correct' requires a measure of 'largest' and a rule for which departures remain acceptable. Without those standards, there is no reproducible assessment. Netskope's report, available November 17, 2026, describes the November 16 attack through a compromised third-party snippet used on sites belonging to 178 brands [e1]. It provides incident context, but neither a historical ranking nor a standard for partial vindication [e1].
limitations: The original Politico article could not be read.
The incident report does not establish that this was the largest cyberattack in history.
Additional incident counts alone cannot define what qualifies as largely correct.
This classification neither validates nor refutes the underlying prediction.
